correctness.rationale: All faces have at most four arcs because both hubs have indegree and outdegree at most one; the four exact face counts are proved by endpoint classification. The stagewise element matching has an earliest-stage acyclicity proof. The exhaustive nine-leaf check decides every low-dimensional face for arbitrary n>=6 by relabeling at most three tail leaves and by the first-six-leaf pivot locality. Thus only top three-cells survive, with their number computed by the alternating face count. For n=5, a separate acyclic matching has one two-cell and 32 three-cells; exact signed integer Morse differential coefficients are 11 copies of +2, 10 of -2 and 11 zero, so the Moore summand and 31 three-spheres follow via integral basis change and pi_2(S^2)=Z. Reproduced standalone checker and mod-2/mod-3 independent chain ranks support the finite certificate; the logical all-parameter transfer is explicit in RESULT.md.

source_inspections.assessment: The ordinary discrete Morse complex has vertices representing graph vertex-edge matched pairs, and imposes at-most-one SOURCE cell per graph vertex, but allows multiple distinct selected oriented edges entering the same target. By contrast, the multipath complex forbids multiple entering arcs. For example, arcs from both hubs into one leaf form a legal discrete Morse matching (two distinct hub-edge pairs) but are forbidden in the multipath complex; the earlier Morse theorem gives n-dimensional spheres, whereas the present complex has top dimension three. Therefore its all-n wedge theorem does not imply the present claim.

value.rationale: The bipartition-(2,n) family is a canonical smallest-width family with directed 2- and 4-cycles, complementing the one-way biclique and bidirected path/polygon literature. The theorem gives a natural full infinite homotopy classification with an exact quartic rank and an integral Moore-space torsion-to-free transition at five versus six leaves. The finite-locality reduction is a reusable mathematical structural mechanism, not a routine numerical table or arbitrary finite slice; five-leaf mod-two homology alone would conceal the attaching degree two.
